title: Spara vs Knock AI vs Storylane RepX (2026)
summary: Spara vs Knock AI compared on channels, qualification, and pricing, with a clear framework for choosing the right inbound AI agent for your GTM motion.
body_markdown:
Here is my honest take after watching dozens of teams stitch together AI qualifiers: the Spara vs Knock AI decision is not about which tool has more features, it is about where your buyer intent actually shows up first. If most of your qualified demand lands on your website one answer wins, and if intent fragments across LinkedIn, Slack, and events before anyone reaches your site the other does. I run marketing at Storylane, so I will also be upfront about where Storylane RepX belongs here and where it does not.


> **Definition:** An inbound AI agent is software that engages a visitor in real time across chat, voice, or messaging, qualifies them against your criteria, and either books a meeting or routes the conversation to a rep, replacing the static lead form and the "we'll get back to you" delay.


Most comparison pages for this query are alternatives listicles or profile pages that mention both tools in passing. None of them actually put Spara and Knock AI side by side and tell you when to choose each. That gap is the whole reason I wrote this.


## TL;DR: Spara vs Knock AI at a glance


Spara and Knock AI both replace forms with AI, but they bet on different surfaces. Spara is website-first: chat, voice, and email agents backed by a private model trained on your sales motion. Knock AI is cross-channel, identifying intent wherever it appears and routing it into messaging tools your reps already use.


A quick "who fits what" summary before the detail:


- **Spara:** heavy website inbound and teams that value on-site voice.
- **Knock AI:** off-site demand capture with messaging-native handoff.
- **Storylane RepX:** teams that want qualification tied to interactive product demos.


One buyer described the target state well:


> "But we're kind of looking for like an agentic marketing solution that, yes, will convert on website visitors, it'll capture intent, and then also has like a... AI agent that works on the website would also book a meeting directly through like a meeting scheduler on the site." - \[Head of Procurement, government / public-sector software\]


That is the job to be done: the rest of this piece is about which tool does it best.


## Quick-reference comparison table


This exact head-to-head does not exist anywhere else in the search results, so here it is. I have added Storylane RepX as a third column because if you are evaluating AI qualifiers, you should see the demo-led option next to the two you searched for, not pretend it is not in the market, since a demo-led qualifier changes the math for product-led teams.


The rows are ordered the way a buyer evaluates, starting with the core motion and ending with the team each tool fits best, so you can stop at the row that decides it for you. Primary motion is the most important line: it tells you where each tool expects intent to originate, and almost everything else follows from that choice. Read the table as a starting hypothesis, not a verdict: every claim in it is unpacked and attributed in the sections below, so nothing here rests on the table alone.

## What is Spara?


Spara is an inbound AI qualifier that runs chat, voice, and email agents on your site. Its defining choice is a private model trained per deployment on your sales motion, brand voice, and qualification criteria, rather than one shared model for every customer. The company has raised roughly $15M in seed funding to build that motion out (Business Wire, 2025).


Beyond qualification, Spara has been expanding into outbound, PLG upsell, AI-guided demos, and event follow-up, so it aims to own more of the funnel than a chat widget. It carries SOC 2 compliance and integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo (Spara, 2026), so it fits a standard mid-market to enterprise stack.


The capability shortlist looks like this:


- Chat, voice, and email agents in one qualifier.
- A per-deployment private model tuned to your criteria.
- Native connections to Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo.
- Expansion into outbound, upsell, and event follow-up.


The nuance that matters for budgeting: Spara typically needs a separate scheduler such as Calendly, Chili Piper, or RevenueHero to book meetings, plus a paid add-on for full-site visitor identification. It is a total-cost-of-stack point I return to under pricing.


## What is Knock AI?


Knock AI is a form-free B2B buyer-engagement platform that engages intent across the website and off-site channels, then qualifies and routes the conversation to a rep. Knock AI reports founding in 2023 and more than $1M in ARR as of late 2025 (Knock AI, 2025), and remains an early-stage team.


Its customers include Fireblocks, Orca Security, Lokalise, and Mixmax (Knock AI, 2026), and its reach across LinkedIn, Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, and website DMs is the point.


Knock AI's capability shortlist:


- Form-free engagement across website and off-site channels.
- Real-time visitor de-anonymization and AI enrichment.
- Native Slack routing that drops qualified buyers into live rep conversations.
- Event lead-capture tools and lightweight CRM sync for faster go-live.


The disambiguation note below matters before you compare further.


### Disambiguation: the B2B Knock AI vs the canvassing "Knock AI"


Quick but important: this article is about the B2B GTM platform at knock-ai.com, not the political door-knocking and canvassing app branded "Knock AI" at knockai.co. They are unrelated products for unrelated buyers, so if you are researching field canvassing software this is the wrong page. I am calling it out because the name collision sends real evaluators to the wrong vendor, and no other comparison page bothers to clear it up.


## Channel coverage compared


Channel strategy is where these two genuinely diverge. Spara concentrates on the website with chat, voice, and email, and voice is its clearest differentiator: very few inbound qualifiers actually talk to a visitor out loud. Knock AI spreads across website DMs plus LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, and iMessage, so its edge is catching intent off-site before it reaches your domain.


Here is the contrast in plain terms:


- **Where Spara is stronger:** on-page depth, on-site voice, and a single qualifier for chat, voice, and email.
- **Where Knock AI is stronger:** off-site reach and messaging-native engagement across many channels.
- **Where they tie:** both aim to replace the static form and both push toward a booked meeting.


Buyers do not want one blunt experience everywhere. One growth leader put the requirement plainly:


> "We were thinking to have one generic one across everywhere. Right. Across all the pages. Just we wanted to have a different flow of chat on demo page and the pricing page and any other high intent page that we categorize later." - \[Founding team, Growth, SaaS\]


That favors whichever tool tailors the flow to where the buyer is.


## Qualification & routing approach


Both tools qualify and route, but the mechanism differs and changes what your reps experience. Spara leans on its per-deployment private model plus cross-channel context, so a chat and a follow-up email are one thread, not three cold starts. Knock AI leans on real-time de-anonymization and intent routing that drops a qualified buyer straight into a live rep conversation.


The practical difference is accuracy versus immediacy: a private model qualifies more precisely over time, while de-anonymization plus Slack routing gets a human in faster. Neither is automatically right; it depends on whether your bottleneck is precision or speed.


Accurate visitor data is the foundation. One demand gen leader made the case for honest counts over vanity numbers:


> "The good and bad about this is it doesn't inflate my numbers. So I have more accurate numbers in the back end than saying, you know, I had 370 anonymous views on the product tour versus I had nine product, you know, known product tour visitors." - \[Head of Demand Generation, SaaS\]


This is where buyer intent becomes a real engagement, so our guide to[digital sales room software](https://www.storylane.io/blog/digital-sales-room-software) covers how to structure that buyer-engagement layer.


## Integrations & setup


Integrations decide whether a tool lives inside your workflow or bolts onto the side. Spara connects to Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo, which covers the common mid-market and enterprise stack, but it usually needs a separate scheduler and a paid add-on for full-site visitor identification. Your integration map therefore includes a booking tool and an identification layer, not just the qualifier.


Knock AI offers CRM sync, native Slack routing, and event lead-capture tools, and reviewers describe a faster, lighter go-live. Its Slack-native handoff is the standout: qualified buyers land where reps already spend their day.


A short setup checklist to run before you sign anything:


1. Confirm which scheduler you will pair with the qualifier, and who owns it.
2. Decide whether you need full-site identification on day one or later.
3. Map the routing destination: CRM record, Slack channel, or both.
4. Pressure-test how each tool handles a visitor across multiple pages and sessions.


One caution from real buyer feedback: an on-site agent can feel intrusive if it is not scoped well. The fix is configuration: scope the agent to high-intent pages and style it to match your brand so it reads as native.


## Pricing compared


Pricing transparency is itself a differentiator here, so I will be blunt about who publishes what. Spara lists tiers around $2,100 and $3,750 per month, which is refreshingly public for this category (Spara, 2026). Knock AI does not publish pricing, so you must request a quote to compare.


The number on the rate card is not your real cost, though. For Spara, the honest total is the license plus a scheduler plus the identification add-on, so model all three before comparing. For Knock AI, the honest total is a quote you have to request, so budget the time to get one.


Cost element Spara Knock AI Storylane RepX


Published price ~$2,100 / ~$3,750 per month Not public Not publicly listed (request a quote)


Scheduler Separate tool (Calendly / Chili Piper / RevenueHero) Included via routing Included in demo flow


Visitor identification Paid add-on for full-site Native de-anonymization Engagement-based signals


Transparency Public tiers Quote-based Quote-based


Compare total cost of stack, not sticker price. A tool with a lower headline number and three required add-ons can easily cost more than a bundled competitor, and a quote-based model also adds a sales cycle before you can even run a pilot. Factor time-to-decision, not just dollars, into the comparison.


## Ratings & real user feedback


Review depth tells you how battle-tested a tool is, and here neither newcomer has much of a public track record yet. Knock AI is the more visible of the two, with early user feedback pointing to its intent routing, de-anonymizer, and Slack handoff as strengths, but its public review base is still thin. Spara's is smaller and newer still, so there is simply less independent signal to lean on.


Fewer reviews does not mean worse, it means less proof, and you should weight that by your risk tolerance. If you need deep social proof today, neither tool has a large public bench yet, so build vendor reference calls into your evaluation. If you are comfortable being an early customer, that thinner track record is not disqualifying for either.


For scale, Storylane carries well over a thousand G2 reviews (G2, 2026), a different maturity tier than either tool here. A small handful of public reviews means you are early in that product's track record.


## Where Storylane RepX fits


Full disclosure: this is us. Storylane RepX is our inbound AI agent, and it makes a deliberately different bet than either Spara or Knock AI. Instead of qualifying inside a chat thread alone, RepX ties the conversation to an interactive product demo, so a buyer can experience the product while the agent qualifies and books time.


The mechanism is simple: engagement and demo behavior become qualification signals, and the meeting gets booked inside the demo flow rather than handed to a separate scheduler. That suits product-led motions where seeing the product is the fastest path to conviction.


Where RepX does not fit: if your core need is off-site capture across LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and Telegram, Knock AI is a more natural home, and if you need on-site voice today, Spara has that edge. RepX is strongest when the demo is the center of your buying experience. On our own pricing I will be straight: it is not publicly listed, so request a quote and model it against your stack like any other line item.


## When to choose Spara vs Knock AI


Map each tool to your situation: your demand pattern, your channels, and how your reps prefer to work.


Choose based on your dominant intent surface:


- **Choose Spara if:** most qualified demand hits your website, you want on-site voice, and you value a private model tuned to your criteria over time.
- **Choose Knock AI if:** intent fragments across LinkedIn, G2, Slack, and events before it reaches your site, and you want messaging-native handoff into live rep conversations.
- **Consider Storylane RepX if:** the interactive demo is the heart of your buying experience and you want qualification tied to product engagement.


Accurate targeting pays off here: engaging the right visitor at the right moment beats blanket coverage. One growth leader framed it well:


> "For example, if somebody has searched for a listicle and landed there organically, might have maybe better chances to have a conversation, get value and get conversion." - \[Founding team, Growth, SaaS\]


Use that lens: the tool that concentrates effort on the visitors most likely to convert is the one to shortlist first.


## Alternatives to consider


Neither Spara nor Knock AI is the only option, and a thorough evaluation should name the adjacent players. Qualified is the Salesforce-native pick for teams that live in that CRM, while Warmly combines inbound and outbound signals on a single graph. Docket, Converzoy, and Breakout round out the field, with Converzoy notable for transparent pricing in a category that mostly hides it.


A short orientation on the field:


- **Qualified:** best if you are Salesforce-native and want tight platform alignment.
- **Warmly:** inbound plus outbound intent on one graph.
- **Converzoy:** transparent pricing, useful for tight-budget evaluations.
- **Docket and Breakout:** adjacent buyer-enablement and qualification options worth a look.


If you want a wider survey of this category before you commit, our roundup of the[top AI SDR tools](https://www.storylane.io/blog/top-ai-sdr-tools) covers the broader landscape and where each tool earns its place. Shortlist two or three, run a real inbound scenario through each, and let your own funnel data decide.


## Choosing between Spara vs Knock AI


The Spara vs Knock AI question comes down to one honest read of your funnel: is your website the front door, or the last stop after intent has already scattered? Spara rewards website-heavy motions and teams that want on-site voice, and Knock AI rewards off-site capture with messaging-native handoff. If the interactive demo is your center of gravity, Storylane RepX deserves a seat at that table too.


Do not buy on feature lists; buy on where your buyers show up, how your reps like to work, and the total cost of the stack you will actually run. My practical suggestion: shortlist the one tool that matches your dominant intent surface, then run a real inbound scenario through it, from first touch to booked meeting, before you commit budget. The tool that wins on your own funnel data, not on a feature grid, is the one to sign, and that verdict can differ by team even when the market looks identical.


## FAQ


**Is Knock AI the same as the canvassing app?**


No. This article covers the B2B GTM platform at knock-ai.com. The political door-knocking and canvassing app branded "Knock AI" at knockai.co is an unrelated product for an unrelated audience.


**Does Spara offer voice?**


Yes, Spara runs chat, voice, and email agents, and on-site voice is one of its clearest differentiators. Very few inbound qualifiers converse out loud, a genuine point of separation from Knock AI.


**Which is cheaper, Spara or Knock AI?**


It depends on your stack. Spara publishes tiers around $2,100 and $3,750 per month, but add a scheduler and a paid identification add-on for the real total. Knock AI is quote-based, so compare total cost of stack, not sticker price.


**Do either replace forms?**


Yes, both do. Spara replaces the static form with website chat, voice, and email qualification, while Knock AI replaces it with form-free engagement across many channels.


**Which integrates with Slack?**


Knock AI offers native Slack routing into live rep conversations. Spara routes through your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo), so if Slack-native handoff is a must-have, Knock AI has the edge.
